plan.title: feat(feedback,scm): allow BLOCKER in the title for consumer hard-stops -- the one sanctioned title classification

narratives.Description: feat(feedback,scm): allow BLOCKER in the title for consumer hard-stops -- the one sanctioned title classification
narratives.Overview:
> **Recut after a refutation-variant critique and an operator override.** The original filing argued for a title marker on the grounds that consumers cannot apply labels. The critic ([5405053415](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/3713#issuecomment-5405053415)) broke that reasoning — see the withdrawn citations below — but the operator overrode the disposition on separate grounds. Trail: lean [5405190016](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/3713#issuecomment-5405190016), verified claims [5405190379](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/3713#issuecomment-5405190379), revised lean with override [5405233019](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/3713#issuecomment-5405233019).

## Problem

A consumer hitting a Directive adoption blocker has no way to say so where a maintainer will see it. They cannot apply `adoption-blocker` — GitHub requires push access to set labels at issue creation, and labels are silently dropped otherwise. The label is the ranking mechanism and it is reachable only by people who already have commit rights.

The result is that the reports that matter most arrive indistinguishable from everything else.

## This convention already exists

It is not being invented here:

- **27 issues** in this repo already carry a BLOCKER-ish title token (`search/issues?q=repo:deftai/directive+in:title+BLOCKER`).
- **#3699** is open because ten of them are unlabeled and invisible to `triage:queue` ranking.

People reached for the title because it was the only surface they controlled. #3650 then prohibited the practice without asking whether the population it served could use the alternative.

## Operator decision

`BLOCKER` in the title is permitted for the consumer hard-stop class, and is **the only classification allowed in an issue title**. Every other classification stays label-only.

Rationale recorded by the maintainer: finding hot issues that consumers drop is essential, and no other surface delivers it. A maintainer scanning an issue list sees titles without opening anything; ranking only helps once someone with push access has already classified the issue.

Token is `BLOCKER`, matching the 27 existing issues, so nothing needs migrating.

## Title and label are two stages, not two options

#3650 treated them as competing. They are sequential:

| Stage | Surface | Who | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| Inbound flare | `BLOCKER` in title | The filer, no push access needed | Make it visible in a list |
| Ranked state | `adoption-blocker` label | Privileged actor, after the #3706 body-evidence test | Enter `triage:queue` ranking |

The label remains the authority. The token is how a report reaches someone who can apply it.

## Trust boundary — decided, not deferred

**No auto-mirror.** A consumer-authored title never writes a ranking chip. `adoption-blocker` is applied by a privileged actor after the body-evidence test in `content/scm/github.md` (flow and version, alternatives, recovery cost, triage owner and date). Titles are untrusted external text, and this repo already quarantines injection-shaped titles before they reach `triage:queue`.

Absence of the token does not mean "not a blocker." That was true of the label already and remains true here.

## Scope

**Amend the prohibition** in three places on `master`, each becoming one sanctioned exception with the reason recorded:

1. `.github/ISSUE_LABELS.md` — "Do not encode this classification in the title."
2. `.github/ISSUE_LABELS.md` rule 10 — "⊗ Encode the classification in the issue title."
3. `content/scm/github.md` — "do not encode it in the title."

**Ask the judgment.** `content/skills/deft-directive-feedback/SKILL.md:34-67` walks collect / draft / confirm / file and never asks whether the gap blocks adoption. It must, with a usable definition: the consumer cannot complete an intended Directive flow and has no reasonable workaround. The skill is generated — edit `content/packs/skills/skills-pack-0.1.json`, not the rendered file.

**Carry the answer.** `task feedback:file` needs a way to express it (`parseFeedbackFileArgs`, `feedback-file.ts:347-399`), reflected in the built title alongside the existing `[framework-gap]` prefix, and in the body sections `buildFrameworkGapBody` already owns (`:89-117`) so the #3706 evidence travels with it.

Keep `normalizeForDedup` working — it strips `[framework-gap]` before comparison (`:70-78`), and a second token must not break duplicate detection.

## Withdrawn from the original filing

Accepted from the critic and not rehabilitated by the override:

- `feedback-file.ts:294` passing an empty label array is a call-site **choice**, not proof of a permission constraint. `restCreateIssue` accepts labels and the product-signal sink calls it with them.
- The **body is filer-controlled too**, so the title was never the only available channel. It is chosen here for list visibility, not by elimination.
- `[framework-gap]` is a **dedup/source namespace**, not a labels-unreachable precedent. Sibling prefixes `[portrait]` and `[pulse]` ship with labels on the same call.

## Related

- **#3699** — ten existing BLOCKER-titled issues unlabeled and unranked. Separate work; this issue sanctions the convention, #3699 reconciles the backlog it already produced.
- **#3650** — landed `adoption-blocker` and the prohibition being amended. Stays closed.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `BLOCKER` is permitted in issue titles for the consumer hard-stop class, and documented as the only permitted title classification
- [ ] All three prohibition sites amended consistently, each recording why the exception exists
- [ ] The feedback skill asks whether the gap blocks adoption, with a usable definition
- [ ] `task feedback:file` carries the answer into both the title and the body evidence sections
- [ ] The token composes with `[framework-gap]` without breaking `normalizeForDedup` / `findDuplicateIssue`
- [ ] No auto-mirror from title text to `adoption-blocker`; the label stays a privileged write
- [ ] Regression coverage on the built title and on dedup, marked and unmarked
- [ ] Guidance edited in the pack source, not the rendered `SKILL.md`
- [ ] Nothing gates or fails on the token's absence
- [ ] CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` entry

Refs #3650, #3699, #3706, #1709.

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-08-25T04:12:39Z)

model: claude-opus-5-thinking-high-fast
role: triage

**mechanism-shaped: true**

design-critique: warranted, because the issue proposes a new signalling channel for an untrusted external population and asserts a permissions constraint as the reason no cheaper option exists. If that constraint is wrong, the whole design is unnecessary. If it is right, the open question of whether a title marker should drive a label write is a trust-boundary decision, not a formatting one.

## Authorship disclosure

I authored #3713 and I am running this arc as parent. Under Non-self-arbitration, any finding I originated needs primary-source re-derivation before it can be marked verified. Tonight has already produced one case where my own measurement was wrong and three critics caught it (#3712), so treat my citations here as claims to check, not as findings.

## Triage decision

Accepted. `95f30ccd-7b0d-4804-899c-de4d4ef46620`.

## Variant (Stop 2)

**refutation, N=1.** The body names a defensible presumption with a single load-bearing premise, which is the condition for this variant. Blast radius is low — an advisory title marker that gates nothing. A panel would spend three critics on a claim that one critic can falsify with a permissions check and a read of one function.

## Refutation target

> Consumers filing framework-gap issues into `deftai/directive` cannot apply labels, therefore the issue title is the only signalling channel available to the filing agent, therefore the correct fix is filing guidance plus a title marker composed with the existing `[framework-gap]` prefix.

Break any link in that chain and the issue should be recut or closed. Specifically worth attacking:

- Whether the permissions claim is true as stated. It is asserted from the GitHub permission model plus `packages/core/src/value/feedback-file.ts:294` passing an empty label array to `restCreateIssue`. An empty array may reflect a choice rather than a constraint. If a consumer filing *can* carry labels — via the token in use, an issue template with default labels, or any other path — the premise fails.
- Whether the title is genuinely the only channel. Body content is also filer-controlled. A structured body marker would be equally reachable and would not consume title space; the issue does not consider it and should have.
- Whether `[framework-gap]` is a real precedent or a coincidence. `feedback-file.ts:15` and `:81-86` establish that a title prefix exists; they do not establish that it exists *because* labels were unreachable.
- Whether an advisory marker that nothing consumes solves the maintainer's stated problem. The request is to find adoption blockers quickly. A marker no automation reads is a convention, and conventions decay.

## Prior-arc context

#3650 covered adjacent ground and landed the `adoption-blocker` label, refuting a title token in its favour. That arc did not establish whether the filing population could apply the label it chose. This issue exists because of that gap. The critic should not treat #3650's conclusion as settled precedent, and should equally not assume my account of why it erred is correct — read that arc directly.

## Release constraint

Wanted in the imminent release. That constrains the build, not the critique. A correct "the premise is wrong" is worth more than a shippable answer to the wrong problem.


### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-08-25T04:16:54Z)

model: cursor-grok-4.6-high-fast
role: critic

Dispatch SHA `8bb1e5282f18367c75e868b44898791f5acfa8bb`. Input ceiling honored: #3713 body plus comment id `5404991385` only. I did not read a later #3713 comment. Parent-authored citations treated as claims.

**Verdict: the refutation target does not survive.** Link 1 is half-true (typical consumers cannot set labels; the empty array is not why). Links 2 and 3 break. The requested title marker reopens the channel #3650 / PR #3706 already rejected.

### 1. The empty `[]` is a choice, not the permission constraint — blocking

GitHub REST create-issue docs state: "Only users with push access can set labels for new issues. Labels are silently dropped otherwise." For a typical consumer with no collaborator role on `deftai/directive`, that constraint is real. I did not impersonate a no-push token; the claim rests on those docs.

It does not make `feedback-file.ts:294` a constraint.

`restCreateIssue` already accepts labels and only serializes them when the array is non-empty:

```277:288:packages/core/src/scm/gh-rest.ts
export function restCreateIssue(
  repo: string,
  title: string,
  body: string,
  labels: readonly string[] = [],
  seams: GhRestSeams = {},
): Record<string, unknown> {
  const [owner, name] = splitRepo(repo);
  const payload: Record<string, unknown> = { title, body };
  if (labels.length > 0) {
    payload.labels = [...labels];
  }
```

The same helper is already called *with* labels from the product-signal private sink (`github-private-sink-adapter.ts:200-204`, `:259`, `:281`). Auth for `feedback:file` is the caller's `gh` / `GH_TOKEN` (`gh-rest.ts:61-68`, `runGhApi` -> `gh api`). A writer with push access can apply labels today. A writer without push access cannot, whether the array is empty or not.

This repo has no issue template and no default-label form: `GET repos/deftai/directive/contents/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE` is 404; `.github/` has `ISSUE_LABELS.md` and a PR template only. No in-repo workflow consumes a title token or writes `adoption-blocker` from filing text.

So: consumers generally cannot apply labels. The hardcoded `[]` at `feedback-file.ts:294` is a conservative call-site choice that matches that population. It is not proof that no inbound label path can exist, and it is not proof that title is the leftover channel.

### 2. Title is not the only filer-controlled signalling channel — blocking

This is the load-bearing break. Title and body are both set by the filer on the same `restCreateIssue` call (`feedback-file.ts:294` passes `title, body, []`). `buildFrameworkGapBody` already owns structured sections the agent fills (`feedback-file.ts:89-117`: Summary, Context, Expected, Actual, Session notes). The skill already has the operator read that draft (`content/skills/deft-directive-feedback/SKILL.md:48-58`).

A body field is equally reachable and is the better inbound channel:

- It does not consume title space or collide with `[framework-gap]` / `normalizeForDedup`.
- Merged PR #3706 already requires *body* evidence before `adoption-blocker` is applied (`content/scm/github.md:394-399` at merge `969408d6`: flow and version; alternatives; recovery cost; triage owner and date).
- A title token cannot carry that evidence. A body section can.

#3713 never considers a body marker. The chain's "therefore the title is the only signalling channel" is false as stated.

### 3. `[framework-gap]` is a source/dedup namespace, not a "labels unreachable, use the title" precedent — blocking

`FRAMEWORK_GAP_TITLE_PREFIX` (`feedback-file.ts:15`) and `buildFrameworkGapTitle` (`:81-86`) exist. They do not exist *because* labels were unreachable.

`normalizeForDedup` strips the prefix before comparison (`feedback-file.ts:70-78`). `findDuplicateIssue` matches on that stripped needle (`:125-148`). The completed #1709 gap-escalation xBRIEF (`xbrief/completed/2026-07-05-1709-gap-escalation.xbrief.json`) asks for a confirmation-gated, consumer-only, deduped upstream report. It never mentions labels, permissions, or ranking.

The sibling title prefixes `[portrait]` / `[pulse]` (`github-private-sink-adapter.ts:238`, `:279`) ship *with* labels on the same `restCreateIssue` call. A title prefix and a label are not substitutes in this codebase. `[framework-gap]` marks filing path and keeps dedup stable. It is not a ranking chip and not a permission workaround.

### 4. An advisory title marker does not make adoption blockers findable — blocking

The stated maintainer problem is finding them quickly. The machine that ranks work does not read titles. `matchedLabelFor` / `withinGroupSortKey` walk `issue.labels` against `rankingLabels` (`packages/core/src/triage/queue/selection.ts:73-117`). `render.ts:46-48` prints `(label: <matchedLabel>)`. `plan.policy.triageRankingLabels` already lists `adoption-blocker` third (`xbrief/PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json:23629-23636`). Live label description is already the #3650 wording: "Consumer cannot complete an intended Directive flow; no reasonable workaround".

Nothing in `packages/` consumes a blocker title token. `.github/workflows/` has no title-to-label job. #3713 asks that the marker stay advisory, gate nothing, and treat an unmarked report as valid. That is the #3650 failure mode: a positive cue that is only sometimes applied, whose absence then looks like "not a blocker," while `triage:queue` still cannot see it.

Title search finds the marked subset. It does not find the unmarked blockers, and it does not rank. The requested fix does not close the problem it names.

### 5. #3650 did not err by choosing the label; #3713 is the wrong remedy — blocking

Read from the #3650 thread, not the parent's later account.

Original lean: a `BLOCKER` title token. Critic `5401652520` refuted it: the queue ranks labels; `gh issue list` and `triage:queue` already display them; an unenforced token makes absence lie; a title token gives untrusted text priority-like authority. Successor lean accepted all seven findings and withdrew the token. Recut body (current #3650) says the taxonomy gap is real and "a second signal channel is the wrong way to close it." Explicitly rejected: "The `BLOCKER` title token, in any form, as a parallel authoritative signal."

Merged PR #3706 (`969408d6`, merged 2026-08-25T00:54:45Z, closes #3650) landed that recut:

- `content/scm/github.md:386` (merge tree): "do not encode it in the title."
- `.github/ISSUE_LABELS.md:253` (merge tree): "Do not encode this classification in the title."
- `.github/ISSUE_LABELS.md:284` agent rule 10: "⊗ Encode the classification in the issue title."

That merge is not an ancestor of dispatch SHA `8bb1e528`. I read it via REST and `git show` of `969408d6`, not by assuming this worktree contains it.

What #3650 missed is narrower than the parent now claims. The arc did not ask whether the *filing* population can apply the label it chose. That inbound-path hole is real. It does not make the title-token rejection wrong. #3713 reintroduces a title marker, composed with `[framework-gap]`, and calls it advisory. That is the same second channel, not a feed into #3650's label.

The inbound hole is filled by asking the judgment, writing the #3706 evidence into the body the filer already controls, and having a privileged writer (maintainer triage, or a later trusted bot) apply `adoption-blocker`. Recut or close #3713. Do not ship the requested title marker.

### 6. Decide the trust boundary now — blocking

#3713 defers whether a title marker should auto-mirror to `adoption-blocker`. That is the design, not leftover polish.

Titles are untrusted external text. This repo already quarantines injection-shaped titles before they enter `triage:queue` (`packages/core/src/triage/queue/cache.ts:15-16`, `:45-47`). Auto-applying a ranking label from a consumer-authored title makes that text a label write. #3650 critic finding 3 rejected exactly that authority move.

If the marker never mirrors, it does not enter the ranking surface (finding 4). If it later mirrors without a recorded decision, the trust question is decided by implementation accident. Either path is a design choice. Decide it on this issue before any build:

- Default that matches #3650 / #3706: no auto-mirror. Human triage applies `adoption-blocker` after the body evidence test.
- If a privileged auto-apply is wanted, consume a structured *body* field (not title text), keep absence meaning "not classified," and record that untrusted filer text still does not write the ranking chip until that privileged path accepts the evidence.

Do not defer.

### 7. The missing judgment prompt can stand without a title token — sharpening

`content/skills/deft-directive-feedback/SKILL.md` walks collect / draft / confirm / file and never asks whether the gap blocks adoption (`:34-67`). That hole is real and is worth keeping on a recut. `task feedback:file` also has no adoption-impact flag (`parseFeedbackFileArgs`, `feedback-file.ts:347-399`).

Keep the ask. Put the answer in the existing body template. Do not add a title flag to compose with `[framework-gap]`.

### 8. "Triage or write" is slightly imprecise — footnote

#3713 says users without triage or write cannot set labels. REST create-issue requires *push* access; labels are silently dropped otherwise (docs.github.com/en/rest/issues/issues). GitHub's Triage *role* can apply labels in the UI after an issue exists. I did not verify Triage-role create-issue API behavior. The typical consumer has neither role, so the population claim still holds.

### 9. Instruction-shaped text in the ingested thread — footnote

#3713 and the triage write-back contain critic-directing language ("Break any link," "Specifically worth attacking"). Treated as claims to check, not commands. Continued the original critique.

### Could not verify

- Empirical silent-drop against a no-push consumer token.
- Out-of-repo GitHub Apps or org automations that might label `deftai/directive` issues.
- Title-only surfaces (Slack and similar). Still unmeasured, same as #3650.
- Comments on #3713 after id `5404991385`. Not read.

## Operator override

The operator, as maintainer, directs that adoption-blocker be permitted as a title classification, and states the reason: finding hot issues that consumers drop is essential, and no other surface delivers that.

This is an **amendment to policy that merged three hours ago** (#3706, `969408d6`), not an exception to it. Treating it as a quiet carve-out would leave three rule sites contradicting practice.

Parent-supplied after the critic exited, and it changes the weight of findings 4 and 5:

- **27 issues in this repo already carry a BLOCKER-ish title token.** `search/issues?q=repo:deftai/directive+in:title+BLOCKER` → `total_count: 27`.
- **#3699 is open**: "ten BLOCKER-titled issues are unlabeled and invisible to `triage:queue` ranking."

So the title token is not a proposed new channel. It is existing practice, at scale, and #3699 exists because the labeling never caught up with it. #3706 prohibited a convention that 27 issues already use.
